questions.question: What is the definition of analogy according to Bloomfield?
questions.solution_html:
• According to Leonard Bloomfield, analogy is the process by which forms are changed
  • to become similar to other forms in the language.
  • To trace sound changes.
  • Explains sound and meaning changes.
  • Assists in reconstructing the parent language.
  • Thus, the Centum-Satam division is an important principle in comparative philology.
  • Pejoration
  • The meaning deteriorates or becomes less favourable.
  • Examples
  •  Villain originally meant farm worker; now it means a wicked person.
  • Cultural developments
  • Latin frater → English brother
  • Importance of Verner's Law
  • Helps reconstruct Proto-Indo-European forms.

questions.question: How the Aryan languages are classified into centum and satam groups?
questions.solution_html:
• The Indo-European (Aryan) languages are divided into Centum and Satam groups
  • based on the development of the original palatal consonants.
  • Centum Group
  • In these languages, the palatal consonants changed into velar sounds (k, g).
  • Examples
  •  Latin
  •  Greek
  •  Celtic
  •  Germanic
  • The word for "hundred" in Latin is centum, pronounced with a "k" sound, hence the
  • name Centum.
  • Satam Group
  • In these languages, the palatal consonants changed into sibilant sounds (s, sh).
  • Examples
  •  Sanskrit
  •  Avestan
  •  Persian
  •  Balto-Slavic languages

questions.question: Explain Verner's law with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Verner's Law was discovered by Karl Verner in 1875. It explains certain exceptions to
  • Grimm's Law in the Germanic languages.
  • Statement of the Law
  • According to Verner's Law, the voiceless fricatives produced by Grimm's Law became
  • voiced when the preceding syllable was not accented in Proto-Indo-European.
  • The changes are
  •  f → b
  •  þ (th) → d
  •  h → g
  •  s → z
  • Examples

  • voiced when the preceding syllable was not accented in Proto-Indo-European.
  • The changes are
  •  f → b
  •  þ (th) → d
  •  h → g
  •  s → z
